  • Method Details

    • controlRobot

      public void controlRobot(uk.ac.warwick.dcs.maze.logic.IRobot robot)
      The main method of the Explorer class that is polled by the maze environment.

      It initialises each run by logging the starting coordinates in startX and startY, and resetting the robotData if this is the first run. Them, based on the exploreMode, it then calls a specific controller for exploring (exploreControl()) or backtracking (backtrackControl()). There are some cases where those controllers decide the other controller must be used, and in that case it calls the other controller.

      This method also does the final facing of the robot. Since, once this method finishes, the run finishes, pollRun is incremented during this method.

      Parameters:
      robot - passed so that the method may use environment properties and methods.
      See Also:

    • exploreControl

      private int exploreControl(uk.ac.warwick.dcs.maze.logic.IRobot robot)
      A controller method that can be selected by the controlRobot() method to choose a direction.

      This method is selected when exploreMode is true. It uses the nonwallExits() method to figure out what kind of location the robot is at, and runs the appropriate handler methods (one of deadEnd(), corridor(), or junction()). There is a case where if the robot is at a dead end, and it is not at the start, it will return a flag (IRobot.CENTRE) signalling this, and change the exploreMode to false.

      Parameters:
      robot - passed so that the method may use environment properties and methods.
      Returns:
      an integer that corresponds to a direction the robot can face towards in the maze environment, or a flag.

    • backtrackControl

      private int backtrackControl(uk.ac.warwick.dcs.maze.logic.IRobot robot)
      A controller method that can be selected by the controlRobot() method to choose a direction.

      This method is selected when exploreMode is false. It uses the nonwallExits() method to figure out what kind of location the robot is at, and runs the appropriate handler methods (one of deadEnd() or corridor(). There is a case where if none of those handler methods are used, then it uses robotData.getLastJunction to get the heading of the robot at that first visit - if robotData returns a flag (IRobot.CENTRE) then it sets exploreMode to true, and returns the flag.

      Else, it checks for the amount of IRobot.PASSAGE exits by looping through all directions and adding to an ArrayList. If the size of the ArrayList is 0, it returns the reverse of the past heading, and removes the junction by calling robotData.removeJunction Else, it follows the same logic that junction() does.

      Parameters:
      robot - passed so that the method may use environment properties and methods.
      Returns:
      an integer that corresponds to a direction the robot can face towards in the maze environment, or a flag.
      See Also:

    • nonwallExits

      private int nonwallExits(uk.ac.warwick.dcs.maze.logic.IRobot robot)
      A method that returns the number of exits that are not walls around the robot in the maze environment.

      It does this by looping through all the directions, looking in each of them, and incrementing a counter if it "sees" a tile that isn't a wall.

      Parameters:
      robot - passed so that the method may use environment properties and methods.
      Returns:
      an integer specifying the amount of non wall exits around the robot in the maze environment.

    • deadEnd

      private int deadEnd(uk.ac.warwick.dcs.maze.logic.IRobot robot)
      A method that handles the robot in the event that it is in a dead end in the maze environment.

      It does so by looping through all directions for the only possible valid direction, and returning this direction.

      Parameters:
      robot - passed so that the method may use environment properties and methods.
      Returns:
      an integer that corresponds to a direction the robot can face towards in the maze environment.

    • corridor

      private int corridor(uk.ac.warwick.dcs.maze.logic.IRobot robot)
      A method that handles the robot in the event that it is in a corridor or corner in the maze environment.

      It does so by searching for the only valid direction (aka non wall) that is not behind it. It checks the front, right, left, and returns the direction that is not a wall.

      Parameters:
      robot - passed so that the method may use environment properties and methods.
      Returns:
      an integer that corresponds to a direction the robot can face towards in the maze environment.

    • junction

      private int junction(uk.ac.warwick.dcs.maze.logic.IRobot robot)
      A method that handles the robot in the event that it is in a junction in the maze environment.

      It does so by first logging the junction in robotData if this is the first time visiting this specific junction. It does so by using the robotData.recordJunction() method.

      Then, it compiles ArrayLists for all unvisited directions and allowed directions by looping through all possible directions and looking if they are walls or beenbefore tiles, and addding those directions to a corresponding ArrayList if the conditions are matched. It then checks how many directions are now in those ArrayLists, and based on the amount it (randomly) returns a direction such that is unvisited if possible, and simply valid if not.

      Parameters:
      robot - passed so that the method may use environment properties and methods.
      Returns:
      an integer that corresponds to a direction the robot can face towards in the maze environment.
      See Also:
      • robotData
      • RobotData.recordJunction(int)

    • beenbeforeExits

      private int beenbeforeExits(uk.ac.warwick.dcs.maze.logic.IRobot robot)
      A function that returns the amount of beenbefore tiles around the robot in the maze environment.

      It calculates this by looping through all the directions, looking in each of them, and incrementing a counter when it "sees" a beenbefore tile.

      Parameters:
      robot - passed so that the method may use environment properties and methods.
      Returns:
      the amount of beenbefore tiles around the robot in the maze environment.

    • reset

      public void reset()
      A function that is called by the maze environment whenever the Reset button is clicked.

      When this happens, it calls robotData.resetJunctionCounter() to reset the counter, and also resets pollRun to 0.
